pictures.scene: Christus, A Goldsmith in His Shop — a goldsmith in a red gown and red cap holding a small hand balance level over a counter strewn with coins, rings and loose jewels, a young couple in black velvet and gold brocade waiting beside him, shelves of silver vessels, coral and beads behind, do not judge, or you will be judged, for with the same judgment you pronounce, you will be judged, and with the measure you use, it will be measured to you
pictures.name: pd_christus_goldsmith

pictures.scene: Millais, Christ in the House of His Parents — a carpenter's shop floored with pale wood shavings, a boy standing at the bench with a wounded palm held out, his mother kneeling before him in blue, an old woman in a red shawl leaning over the bench and a bearded carpenter bending in from the right, why do you look at the speck in your brother's eye, but fail to notice the beam in your own eye, how can you say to your brother, let me take the speck out of your eye, while there is still a beam in your own eye
pictures.name: pd_millais_carpenter

pictures.scene: Teniers, The Blind Leading the Blind — a blind man in a brown coat groping forward with a staff and a pewter tankard while a boy in a white shirt steers him by the belt, another man already fallen into the ditch at the right, a small child at the left and a shepherd with his sheep beyond the trees, you hypocrite, first take the beam out of your own eye, and then you will see clearly to remove the speck from your brother's eye, do not give dogs what is holy, do not throw your pearls before swine
pictures.name: pd_teniers_the_blind_leading_the_blind

pictures.scene: Snyders, Fighting Dogs — hounds tearing at each other on open ground under a bright sky, a white spotted dog lunging with its paw on a tawny dog's back and its jaws open, a grey-muzzled dog biting in from the right, if you do, they may trample them under their feet, and then turn and tear you to pieces, ask, and it will be given to you, seek, and you will find, knock, and the door will be opened to you
pictures.name: pd_snyders_dogs_fighting

pictures.scene: Melendez, Still Life with Figs and Bread — cut loaves and round rolls heaped on a plain table beside a white dish piled with green and purple figs, a dark glass bottle, a small wooden barrel and a knife laid at the edge, for everyone who asks receives, he who seeks finds, and to him who knocks, the door will be opened, which of you, if his son asks for bread, will give him a stone
pictures.name: pd_melendez_figs_and_bread

pictures.scene: van Beijeren, Still Life with Fish — silver-scaled fish and a cut steak of salmon heaped together in a wicker basket on a wooden bench, a knife lying beside them and a copper pot behind in the shadow, or if he asks for a fish, will give him a snake, so if you who are evil know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more will your father in heaven give good things to those who ask him
pictures.name: pd_beijeren_stilleven_met_vissen

pictures.scene: Bauernfeind, A Gate in Jerusalem — a wide sunlit stone archway thrown across a crowded street with latticed windows above it, an old man in a white headcloth leaning on a staff in the glare, a boy in a red coat with a dog, traders and seated figures waiting in the shadow of the arch, in everything, then, do to others as you would have them do to you, for this is the essence of the law and the prophets, enter through the narrow gate, for wide is the gate and broad is the way that leads to destruction, and many enter through it
pictures.name: pd_bauernfeind_jerusalem_gate

pictures.scene: Harpignies, The Path — a narrow dirt track climbing away uphill beneath one great dark tree, a white stream rushing over stones beside it and green wooded hills closing in beyond, but small is the gate and narrow the way that leads to life, and only a few find it, beware of false prophets, they come to you in sheep's clothing, but inwardly they are ravenous wolves
pictures.name: pd_harpignies_weg

pictures.scene: Pissarro, Orchard in Blossom at Louveciennes — a fruit tree standing in full white blossom against a blue sky with scattered cloud, bare brown earth turned over beneath it and a figure in blue stooping at work among the trees at the left, by their fruit you will recognize them, are grapes gathered from thornbushes, or figs from thistles, likewise, every good tree bears good fruit, but a bad tree bears bad fruit
pictures.name: pd_pissarro_orchard_in_bloom_louveciennes

pictures.scene: van der Neer, Fire at Night — a town burning in the dark, orange flame and rolling smoke lighting the clouds and the church tower above a drawbridge, the black water carrying the glare and small dark figures watching helpless from the bank, a good tree cannot bear bad fruit, and a bad tree cannot bear good fruit, every tree that does not bear good fruit is cut down and thrown into the fire
pictures.name: pd_van_der_neer_nocturnal_fire

pictures.scene: Van Gogh, Olive Trees — old olive trunks twisting up out of ground laid in orange, yellow and blue strokes, their blue-green foliage filling the upper half of the canvas and one small figure in orange bending at work beneath them, so then, by their fruit you will recognize them, not everyone who says to me, lord, lord, will enter the kingdom of heaven, but only he who does the will of my father in heaven
pictures.name: pd_van_gogh_olive_trees

pictures.scene: Fra Angelico, The Last Judgement — Christ enthroned in a blue mandorla against a gold ground with his hand raised in judgment, ranks of haloed saints and apostles seated either side of him, angels kneeling in prayer at his feet and one angel below holding up the cross, many will say to me on that day, lord, lord, did we not prophesy in your name, and in your name drive out demons and perform many miracles, then i will tell them plainly, i never knew you, depart from me, you workers of lawlessness
pictures.name: pd_fra_angelico_the_last_judgement

pictures.scene: Schinkel, Gothic Church on a Rock by the Sea — a great spired cathedral standing dark on the crown of a wooded crag above the water, its buttresses and pinnacles cut sharp against a sky banded with pink and gold at sunrise, a small cross on the rock below it, therefore everyone who hears these words of mine and acts on them is like a wise man who built his house on the rock, the rain fell, the torrents raged, and the winds blew and beat against that house, yet it did not fall, because its foundation was on the rock
pictures.name: pd_schinkel_gothic_church_on_a_rock_by_the_sea

pictures.scene: Schelfhout, The Ruins of Brederode — the broken brick keep of a castle standing roofless and overgrown among summer trees, grass sprouting along its torn wall tops, a tiled cottage roof leaning against its foot and a woman in a red skirt and white cap walking the sandy path below with her dog, but everyone who hears these words of mine and does not act on them is like a foolish man who built his house on sand, the rain fell, the torrents raged, and the winds blew and beat against that house, and it fell, and great was its collapse
pictures.name: pd_schelfhout_ruine_brederode

pictures.scene: Bruegel, The Sermon of Saint John the Baptist — a huge crowd packed together on the floor of a wood to hear one preacher in a brown robe speaking with his hands open, hundreds of faces in hoods, white kerchiefs and broad straw hats turned toward him, men climbed into the branches above to see over the heads, when jesus had finished saying these things, the crowds were astonished at his teaching, because he taught as one who had authority, and not as their scribes
pictures.name: pd_bruegel_the_sermon_of_saint_john_the_baptist

lines.text: Do not judge, or you will be judged.
For with the same judgment you pronounce, you will be judged; and with the measure you use, it will be measured to you.
Why do you look at the speck in your brother's eye, but fail to notice the beam in your own eye?
How can you say to your brother, Let me take the speck out of your eye, while there is still a beam in your own eye?
You hypocrite! First take the beam out of your own eye, and then you will see clearly to remove the speck from your brother's eye.
Do not give dogs what is holy; do not throw your pearls before swine.
If you do, they may trample them under their feet, and then turn and tear you to pieces.
Ask, and it will be given to you; seek, and you will find; knock, and the door will be opened to you.
For everyone who asks receives; he who seeks finds; and to him who knocks, the door will be opened.
Which of you, if his son asks for bread, will give him a stone?
Or if he asks for a fish, will give him a snake?
So if you who are evil know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more will your Father in heaven give good things to those who ask Him!
In everything, then, do to others as you would have them do to you. For this is the essence of the Law and the Prophets.
Enter through the narrow gate. For wide is the gate and broad is the way that leads to destruction, and many enter through it.
But small is the gate and narrow the way that leads to life, and only a few find it.
Beware of false prophets. They come to you in sheep's clothing, but inwardly they are ravenous wolves.
By their fruit you will recognize them. Are grapes gathered from thornbushes, or figs from thistles?
Likewise, every good tree bears good fruit, but a bad tree bears bad fruit.
A good tree cannot bear bad fruit, and a bad tree cannot bear good fruit.
Every tree that does not bear good fruit is cut down and thrown into the fire.
So then, by their fruit you will recognize them.
Not everyone who says to Me, Lord, Lord, will enter the kingdom of heaven, but only he who does the will of My Father in heaven.
Many will say to Me on that day, Lord, Lord, did we not prophesy in Your name, and in Your name drive out demons and perform many miracles?
Then I will tell them plainly, I never knew you; depart from Me, you workers of lawlessness!
Therefore everyone who hears these words of Mine and acts on them is like a wise man who built his house on the rock.
The rain fell, the torrents raged, and the winds blew and beat against that house; yet it did not fall, because its foundation was on the rock.
But everyone who hears these words of Mine and does not act on them is like a foolish man who built his house on sand.
The rain fell, the torrents raged, and the winds blew and beat against that house, and it fell, and great was its collapse!
When Jesus had finished saying these things, the crowds were astonished at His teaching,
because He taught as one who had authority, and not as their scribes.
